questions.def: Use 'a' before singular countable nouns starting with a consonant sound.
questions.question: I want to buy ___ new car next year.

questions.def: Use 'an' before words that start with a vowel sound.
questions.question: He is ___ honest man, believe me.

questions.def: 'News' is uncountable, so no article is needed before the adjective.
questions.question: There is ___ news on TV tonight. (important)

questions.def: Use 'the' for specific places like 'the gym'.
questions.question: I go to ___ gym three times a week.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a specific item.
questions.question: Can you pass me ___ salt, please?

questions.def: It should be 'an idea'.
questions.question: I have a idea to go to beach.

questions.def: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: He works as ___ engineer. (electrical)

questions.def: Use 'the' with superlatives like 'tallest'.
questions.question: She is ___ tallest girl in the class.

questions.def: Use 'a' for a singular countable noun that is not specific.
questions.question: They live in ___ small house near the river.

questions.def: It should be 'an interesting film'.
questions.question: I saw the interesting film last night.

questions.def: Superlatives like 'best' require the definite article 'the'.
questions.question: He is ___ best student. (a)

questions.def: Do not use an article with uncountable nouns used generally.
questions.question: I don't eat ___ meat.

questions.def: Use 'the' when going to a place for a specific purpose.
questions.question: He went to ___ school yesterday.

questions.def: Advice is uncountable, use 'a piece of'.
questions.question: I need a piece of an advice.

questions.def: Even though it starts with 'u', it sounds like 'y', so use 'a'.
questions.question: She is ___ university student. (a)

questions.def: Use 'the' for unique things like capitals.
questions.question: What is ___ capital of France?

questions.def: Use 'the' with plural geographical features like 'mountains'.
questions.question: They went to ___ mountains last winter.

questions.def: Use 'a' before singular countable nouns that are not specific.
questions.question: She has ___ cat. (a)

questions.def: Use 'a' before a singular, countable noun starting with a consonant.
questions.question: He is ___ doctor.

questions.def: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound (silent 'h').
questions.question: I need ___ hour to finish the work.

questions.def: Use 'an' before words that begin with a vowel sound.
questions.question: I have ___ apple. (an)

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to musical instruments.
questions.question: He plays ___ guitar very well.

questions.def: Use 'a' for a singular countable noun that is not specific.
questions.question: She is ___ student at the local college.

questions.def: I go to work (no article) is the correct form.
questions.question: I go to the work every day early.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a specific thing previously mentioned.
questions.question: This is ___ book I was telling you about. (the)

questions.def: No article is needed when talking about tea in general.
questions.question: I like to drink ___ tea in the morning.

questions.def: Use 'a' because 'European' starts with a consonant sound.
questions.question: He is ___ European.

questions.def: Use 'a' before singular, countable nouns starting with a consonant sound.
questions.question: I want to buy ___ new car next year.

questions.def: Use 'an' before singular, countable nouns starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: He is ___ honest man.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a specific, known place.
questions.question: We went to ___ cinema last night. (the)
